seo.metaTitle: YouTube Hashtag Generator: The Three That Show
seo.metaDescription: Generate YouTube hashtags with the first three chosen carefully, since those are the only ones shown above your title. Free, no login.

intro: YouTube hashtags work in a way that catches almost everyone out. Only the first three appear as clickable links above your video title, and those three are the ones anyone will ever see or press. Everything past them sits in the description doing very little. Worse, there is a hard rule most people do not know: use more than fifteen hashtags on a video and YouTube ignores all of them, including the first three. This generator is built around those two facts, so it leads with a small set and tells you which ones are actually going to be visible.
howto: Describe your video in the words someone would type to find it. YouTube is a search engine before it is a feed, so plain search language works better than clever phrasing.
Check the topic match and correct it if needed.
Leave the count at three. That is how many appear above your title, and it is the only number that changes what viewers see.
Press Build. The first group is the visible three, so make sure those are the clearest terms for your subject.
Copy them into the end of your description. They appear above the title automatically once they are in the description.
benefits: Leading with three rather than fifteen is the difference between a tool that understands YouTube and one that has been ported from Instagram. Fifteen tags on a YouTube video achieve almost nothing except risking the limit that switches them all off. The interface here says so plainly, so anyone using it learns the rule rather than repeating the mistake.

The groups are also labelled for what YouTube does with them: the visible three, the ones that only sit in the description, and the specific ones worth adding only if they genuinely fit. That framing matters because it points attention at the parts of a YouTube video that actually drive views, which are the title, the thumbnail and the first fifteen seconds. Hashtags are a small tidying job by comparison, and knowing that is worth more than another twelve tags.
useCases: Creators uploading tutorials and how-to content get the most from this, because those videos are found through search and the three visible tags reinforce the subject. Anyone running Shorts uses it too, where hashtags carry slightly more weight because there is less metadata to go on.

It is also useful for channels that have been adding long hashtag lists for years without knowing about the fifteen limit, which is a surprisingly common situation and an easy fix. If you publish the same content elsewhere, our [general hashtag generator](/tools/hashtag-generator/) covers every platform, and the [hashtag counter](/tools/hashtag-counter/) will warn you when a description crosses the limit.

faqs.q: How many hashtags should I use on YouTube?
faqs.a: Three. Only the first three appear above your title, and those are the only ones viewers see or click. Adding more does not extend that; it just fills your description.

faqs.q: What happens if I use more than 15 hashtags?
faqs.a: YouTube ignores all of them, including the first three, and in some cases the upload is flagged. This is a documented rule rather than a theory, and it is the single most useful thing to know about YouTube hashtags.

faqs.q: Where do I put the hashtags?
faqs.a: At the end of the video description. YouTube pulls the first three from there and displays them above the title automatically. You can also put one in the title itself, though that usually looks worse than it reads.

faqs.q: Do hashtags help a video rank?
faqs.a: Only a little, and far less than the title, the description text and the thumbnail. They help YouTube place the video in a subject and give viewers a route to related content. Treat them as tidying rather than as a growth lever.

faqs.q: Are hashtags more important on Shorts?
faqs.a: Slightly, because a Short carries less surrounding text for YouTube to read, so the tags are a larger share of what it has. The same three-visible rule and fifteen limit still apply.
